nary_nodes.label: Los Angeles Lakers sale to Iger and Kushner
evidence: In a stunning twist, former Disney CEO Bob Iger and venture capitalist Josh Kushner are buying one of the greatest trophy assets in US sports: The Los Angeles Lakers.
The sale comes less than a year after the NBA approved billionaire Mark Walter as the storied franchise’s majority owner.
Iger and Kushner confirmed the deal... in a statement on Wednesday.
The deal still needs the approval of the NBA’s Board of Governors to be completed.

nary_nodes.label: Iger and Kushner on Lakers stewardship
evidence: "As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world," Iger and Kushner said in the statement. "Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."

nary_nodes.label: Mark Walter’s majority ownership of Lakers
evidence: Mark Walter, whose Guggenheim Investments, owns the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team, bought a majority interest in the Lakers in a deal announced just over a year ago.
That deal valued the team at $10 billion, although Walter did not buy 100% ownership. He has run the team since last October.

nary_nodes.label: Mark Walter on Lakers ownership
evidence: "Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life – an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family," Walter said in statement to ESPN.

nary_nodes.label: Guggenheim Investments federal investigation
evidence: News of the sale comes as Walter’s financial business is mired in legal trouble.
Late last month, The Wall Street Journal reported an internal whistleblower complaint about Walter’s Guggenheim Investments triggered a federal investigation.

CNN has not independently confirmed the investigation, and a spokesperson for Guggenheim’s parent company told the Journal they have "always acted in good faith," are cooperating with authorities and are confident it will get "resolved favorably."
